access.edition_or_version: Upanisads, trans. Patrick Olivelle (Oxford World's Classics, 1996)

mechanics.premise: The nature of the self and of ultimate reality taught through teacher-student dialogue.
mechanics.argumentative_stance: Gradual generalisation: a concrete lesson or experiment is drawn toward an abstract claim about self and being.
mechanics.point_of_view: Dialogue between guru and student (e.g., Uddalaka and Svetaketu); the questioner's understanding models the reader's.
mechanics.structure: Serial teaching exchanges, each building a concept through question, analogy and repetition of a refrain.
mechanics.dialogue: Question-and-answer leading the student to infer the principle rather than receive it as a proposition.
mechanics.imagery: Domestic experiment and natural analogy (salt in water, seed, rivers) embodying abstract identity claims.
mechanics.critical_reception: One of the principal early Upanisads; a standard example of dialogic philosophical instruction.
mechanics.failure_or_misuse_signals: Analogy left unexplained, or instruction with no inferential step, becomes dogma rather than philosophy.
